title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). This is the 'modular case' of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. S is a base, eventually the absolute base Z. G is a form of GL(2)_S, with determinant to G_m, centre G_m and adjoint quotient P(G) = PGL-type. SG is the derived (SL-type) subgroup. T_rho and T_sigma are '+-toric' group schemes 'in the air' with epimorphisms delta_rho, delta_sigma onto G_m. They are modelled on the unit groups of Z[rho] and Z[i]: T_rho(Z) = Z/6 and T_sigma(Z) = Z/4, the stabilisers of the two elliptic points of the modular curve. M_{rho,sigma} is a group scheme mapping to G x Z x Z, and M°_{rho,sigma} is its neutral component, mapping to G. The previous page builds Gamma° := M°/G^+_{rho,sigma}, where G^+_{rho,sigma} is a copy of SG inside M°, and identifies Gamma° with T_rho x_{G_m} T_sigma.

What this page does.
(1) There is a morphism from the 'torus' T°_{rho,sigma} = T_rho x_{G_m} T_sigma into M°_{rho,sigma}. Composing with M° -> G gives a homomorphism T_rho x_{G_m} T_sigma -> G. It factors as the canonical epimorphism onto G_m (the common value of delta_rho and delta_sigma), followed by the monomorphism i_G: G_m -> G, the inclusion of the centre (scalars). So its image is the central torus.
(2) Remark on the non-connected group. Let R** be the inverse image of G_m x Z x Z under M_{rho,sigma} -> G x Z x Z. Its intersection with G^+_{rho,sigma} (isomorphic to SG) is G_m ∩ SG = centre of SG = mu_2. One has R°_{rho,sigma} = R** ∩ M°_{rho,sigma} = (R**)°, the neutral component. A crossed-out passage contemplates renaming (R~ for R, the old R becoming R°, SR becoming SR°). He declines to make R** explicit in terms of T_rho, N_sigma, since it may not be needed.
(3) Marginal NB. R_{rho,sigma} is simply the kernel of Theta: M_{rho,sigma} -> G -> P(G) (ref. (67)). This gives the exact sequence (81): 1 -> R_{rho,sigma} -> M_{rho,sigma} -> P(G) -> 1. The kernel of the composite to P(G) is the inverse image of the centre G_m, so this R is the R** of the remark, which explains the abandoned renaming.

Purpose. This prepares the computation on the next page. There SR°(Z) ≅ T_rho(Z) x T_sigma(Z) = Z/6 x Z/4, and R°(Z) ≅ (Z/6 x Z/4) x {±1}, with the {±1} factor the centre mu_2 of SG. This is a group-scheme ('arithmetic') incarnation over Z of the elliptic-point stabilisers, i.e. of the data behind SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 and the modular orbifold's fundamental groupoid with base points rho and sigma.
errors: Surjectivity of M_{rho,sigma} -> P(G) in (81) is asserted without argument. It is plausible if M contains a copy of SG mapping onto P(G) fppf-locally, since SG -> PG is an fppf epimorphism with kernel mu_2. It is not a surjection on Z-points.
The equation number (81) in the margin is reused on the next page for a different formula; this is a numbering clash, not a mathematical error.
Minor: the statement R** ∩ M° = (R**)° needs R** ∩ M° to be connected. That holds because it is an extension of a torus by a torus-like piece, but this is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Factorisation of T_rho x_{G_m} T_sigma -> M° -> G through the canonical epimorphism to G_m followed by the inclusion of the centre
ideas.modern_name: fibre product of norm-type tori over G_m; central torus of GL2

ideas.what: R_{rho,sigma} as kernel of M -> G -> PG, with exact sequence 1 -> R -> M -> P(G) -> 1
ideas.modern_name: inverse image of the centre / kernel of the adjoint map

ideas.what: Group schemes over Z encoding the elliptic-point stabilisers Z/6 and Z/4 (tori T_rho, T_sigma attached to Z[rho], Z[i]) and their gluing over the centre mu_2 of SL2
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic model of the amalgam SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6; tori of CM points in GL2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Trees) for the amalgam; CM tori classical
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the Longue Marche (1981) discussion of the modular case; unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck deliberately leaves unwritten the explicit construction of R** (= R_{rho,sigma}) in terms of T_rho, N_sigma (the normaliser) etc., i.e. a group-scheme model of the full non-connected group. This is part of a larger unpublished programme of group schemes over Z modelling the modular 'loop equation'. The page itself only contains routine steps of it.
missed.quote: Je ne vais pas expliciter ici la construction de R**_{rho,sigma} en termes des T_rho, N_sigma etc, n'étant pas sûr qu'il y en aura besoin par la suite.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is marginally relevant to schematic/arithmetic models of SL2(Z) and of the fundamental groupoid of M_{1,1} with tangential base points at the elliptic points. The step itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of routine bookkeeping: a factorisation through the centre, a neutral-component identity and a kernel description, inside a larger unpublished construction. Nothing here is a new result.
transcription_corrections: Subscripts written 'G_ss' should read 'G_m' (Grothendieck writes 'Gm'): T_rho x_{G_m} T_sigma -> G_m -> G via i_G.
First line: the fibre product is over G_m, not G, consistent with the previous page.
'image inverse de G_ss x Z x Z' should read 'de G_m x Z x Z'.
'évidemment égale à Z' is almost certainly 'égale à mu_2' (centre of SG). The next page confirms the mu_2 = {±1} factor.
'dans l'intersection avec G^+_{rho,sigma} ≃ SG' — the symbol after ≃ is SG.
Margin: 'Theta: M_{rho,sigma} -> G -can-> P(G)'; the reference '(67)' points to an earlier formula.
